endorsements.quote: AI agent decisions should be revisable, questionable, and rejectable by a human-in-the-loop (e.g., practitioner, patient, proxy), whose identity must be recorded to address legal accountability and clinical responsibility.
Explicit human override conditions should be defined and human intervention triggered, when predefined clinical thresholds (e.g., high-risk interventions, irreversible outcomes) are exceeded.

unlisted_practices: Require every medical AI agent to consult an Ethical Reasoning Module that reviews the agent's decisions from an ethical viewpoint and produces a structured, auditable record of inputs, outputs, reasoning traces, and intermediate agent exchanges.
Subject Ethical Reasoning Modules to regulatory approval by appropriate governing bodies.

Design AI agents to incorporate structured patient preference profiles (advance directives, values surveys, optional ethical stance questionnaires) while retaining real-time patient feedback for dynamic adaptation.
Adapt institutional ethics committees to assess AI agents' decisions with the same rigor used to review human practitioners' actions.
Provide ethics committees with maintained domain-specific review tools, structured evaluation templates, and training, regularly updated and streamlined to avoid bureaucratic bottlenecks.
Establish a centralized open-access repository of diverse real-world and fictional ethical scenarios, curated by a neutral, representative international consortium.
Develop benchmarking tools for longitudinal evaluation of AI agents' ethical reasoning, in development and after deployment, enforced by national regulatory bodies with a structured update mechanism.
Develop shared guidance on regulatory sandbox criteria to support transparency and comparability across health systems.
National supervisory authorities should adapt existing accountability mechanisms so they are applicable and enforceable for AI systems.
Establish legal mechanisms that enforce and incentivize adherence to ethical principles by AI agents.

screen.reason: This is a framework/perspective preprint proposing six practical interventions/governance mechanisms for ethical implementation of medical AI agents, not an empirical study.
